result.behaviour_summary: backtest.run() now appends two additive columns at the end of the trades frame (the one write_run stores as trades.csv.gz): matched_mean_net_return and same_session_mean_net_return. Each is reduced from the raw draw dict the run already executes (raw["random_matched"] / raw["random"], net_return reshaped to (draws, attempts)): the mean over the draws whose net_return is finite, i.e. the scored controls (execution.execute sets net_return to NaN for every unscored status). The value is placed at the attempted signals' positions via the existing `attempt` mask, so overlap-skipped signals (which draw no controls) are NaN; signals none of whose draws was scored are NaN; when no signal is attempted (raw is empty) the columns exist and are empty. _baseline, dist(), the same-session and matched draw generation, the by_year block, summary and draws_df are untouched. In an as_traded run the two columns come after the *_as_traded columns, still at the end. paired_excess(trades_df) computes per-signal excess = net_return - matched_mean_net_return over rows where both are finite (so only scored, attempted trades with a scored control mean enter), groups them by signal_date, and bootstraps the mean excess by resampling clusters with replacement (10,000 resamples, seed 20261015 by default, numpy default_rng, fixed 1000-resample chunks so the stream is independent of memory heuristics; mean of a resample = sum of cluster sums / sum of cluster counts). p_one_sided for mean excess > 0 is (1 + #(resampled means <= 0)) / (1 + resamples), the same +1 convention as the harness's dist(); ci95 is the 2.5/97.5 percentile of the resampled means. The module docstring describes the columns and the statistic. Nothing in summary.json reports the new statistic: it is for a caller (e5.py) to compute from output["trades"] and record.

Nothing in backtest.run or summary.json reports the statistic by design (summary unchanged).

research/E5/protocol.json (frozen by its owner): if the protocol wants the per-signal count of scored control draws alongside the mean (useful to see how many of the 200 draws were skipped on illiquid names), that would be a further additive column in backtest.py; not added because the task specified exactly two columns.
open_concerns: Definition choice: the control mean is over the draws that were scored (net_return finite); unscored draws (SKIP_*, INCOMPLETE, corporate-action exclusions) are left out of the mean rather than counted as zero. This is the only definable mean given execute() returns NaN net returns for them, and it mirrors _summary_stats; a protocol reader should know a signal whose controls were mostly skipped has a mean over fewer than 200 draws.

paired_excess uses the harness's (1 + count) / (1 + resamples) one-sided p, so the minimum p is 1/(1 + resamples) (about 1e-4 at 10,000); the draft protocol's text says 'one-sided p' without fixing the +1 convention. ci95 is the plain percentile interval of the resampled means (no bias correction).

Cluster keys are compared as strings of the signal_date column; in a harness trades frame signal_date is already an ISO string per row, so this is exact. A caller passing a frame with a datetime column gets equivalent clustering.

In an as_traded run (units='as_traded') the two columns follow the three *_as_traded columns, i.e. the frame's last two columns in every configuration; any consumer should select by name, not position (none in-repo selects by position).

The clone test asserts the summary's matched random_mean equals rule_trades.avg_net_return only to 12 places: the two are the same numbers summed in a different order (per-draw means then across draws vs across trades), a pre-existing last-ulp difference, not something this change introduced.
The untracked .githooks/* files in the worktree were there before this task and are not mine; they were not added to the commit.
Nothing here is a performance claim: all numbers in the tests and the comparison script come from synthetic random-walk panels.
